instructions.content: NEVER write a claim into "What We Found" without a citation, no matter how plausible it sounds.
NEVER cite the code itself as evidence for why it exists; motivation only comes from an external source.
NEVER assume the most recent commit is the authoritative reason for the current shape; trace back.
NEVER treat a hypothesis embedded in the user's own question as already confirmed; check it against the evidence independently.
NEVER omit the "What We Don't Know" section, even when the investigation felt thorough.
NEVER skip an investigator because you assume its category won't have anything; a null result is a data point, a skipped search is a blind spot.
NEVER pool multiple evidence categories into a single investigator agent; always one investigator per category.
Establish the code anchor first (tokensave_blame/tokensave_log for structural history, PR/MR context where a remote exists) before spawning any investigator.
Spawn one investigator per available evidence category in a single concurrent message, each given the base investigator prompt plus its category's playbook.
The synthesizer tiers every claim as Direct/Supported/Inferred/Speculative/Unknown and produces a Sources Consulted coverage map naming what was searched, found empty, or skipped and why.
Prefer hedged language ("appears to", "likely") for inferred claims; reserve confident language ("because") for direct, explicit evidence only.
Prefer presenting competing hypotheses with evidence for and against each over forcing a single winner when the record doesn't clearly support one.
